Heatmap der diagnostischen CpGs
```{r}
#Library pheatmap and brewer.pal
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)

#Adding color to tissue type 
annotation_color <- list(Type=c(`Primary solid Tumor`='red', `Solid Tissue Normal` = 'blue'))

#Heatmap complete linkage
pheatmap(cpgs_for_BRCA_diagnosis_data, 
         show_rownames = FALSE, 
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         annotation_col = tissue_types, 
         annotation_colors=annotation_color,
         color=colorRampPalette(c("maroon4", "white", "darkgreen"))(100))
```

```{r}
#diagnostic BRCA cpgs for spesific tissue
healthy_patients <- cpgs_for_BRCA_diagnosis_data[,BRCA_sample_sheet$Type == 'Solid Tissue Normal'] 
healthy_patients
```

```{r}
tumor_patients <- cpgs_for_BRCA_diagnosis_data[,BRCA_sample_sheet$Type == 'Primary solid Tumor'] 
print(tumor_patients)
```


Violinplots für diagnostische CpGs mit Signifikanz 

```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(ggpubr)

# Creating long format for violinplot 
healthy_long <- melt(as.matrix(healthy_patients), varnames = c("CpG", "PatientID"), value.name = "Methylation")
healthy_long$Status <- 'Solid Tissue Normal'

tumor_long <- melt(as.matrix(tumor_patients), varnames = c("CpG", "PatientID"), value.name = "Methylation")
tumor_long$Status <- 'Primary solid Tumor'

# combine both long formats
combined_data <- rbind(healthy_long, tumor_long)
print(combined_data)
```

```{r}
# Checking normality with Shapiro-Wilk test for methylation levels of a specific CpG site
check_normality <- function(data) {
  shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(data)
  p_value <- shapiro_test$p.value
  is_normal <- shapiro_test$p.value > 0.05
  return(list(p_value = p_value, is_normal = is_normal))
}

# Significance test
display_significance <- function(p_value) {
  if (p_value < 0.001) {
    return("***")
  } else if (p_value < 0.01) {
    return("**")
  } else if (p_value < 0.05) {
    return("*")
  } else {
    return("")
  }
}

# Plots for each cpg with significance
unique_cpgs <- unique(combined_data$CpG)

for (cpg in unique_cpgs) {
  # extract dta for each cpg from data
  data <- subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg)$Methylation
  group <- subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg)$Status
  
  
  # check normality
  normality <- check_normality(data)
  
  # "significance" is created and set to an empty string
  significance <- ""
  
  if (normality$is_normal) {
    # t-Test 
    t_test_result <- t.test(data ~ group)
    p_value <- t_test_result$p.value
    test_result <- t_test_result$statistic
    test_name <- "t-test"
    
    # show significance
    significance <- display_significance(p_value)
  } else {
    # Mann-Whitney-U-Test 
    mwu_test_result <- wilcox.test(data ~ group)
    p_value <- mwu_test_result$p.value
    test_result <- mwu_test_result$statistic
    test_name <- "Mann-Whitney-U-test"
    
    # show significance with star
    significance <- display_significance(p_value)
  }
  
# In Ihrem Schleifenblock, wo Sie die Daten für jeden CpG-Bereich verarbeiten:
group <- factor(subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg)$Status, levels = c("Solid Tissue Normal", "Primary solid Tumor"))

# Dann verwenden Sie group in ggplot:
p <- ggplot(subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg), aes(x = group, y = Methylation, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Solid Tissue Normal" = "blue", "Primary solid Tumor" = "red")) +
  labs(title = paste("Methylation Levels for", cpg, "\n", test_name, "p-value =", p_value, significance), x = "Status", y = "Methylation Level") +
  theme_minimal()

  
  # show plot
  print(p)
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0("plots/ViolinPlot_", cpg, ".pdf"), plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
}
  



```

Boxplots für diagnostische CpGs

```{r}
significance_labels <- data.frame(CpG = character(), Significance = character(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# Calculate significance for each CpG site and store the results
for (cpg in unique_cpgs) {
  # Extract data for each CpG
  data <- subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg)$Methylation
  group <- subset(combined_data, CpG == cpg)$Status
  
  # Check normality
  normality <- check_normality(data)
  
  if (normality$is_normal) {
    # t-Test 
    t_test_result <- t.test(data ~ group)
    p_value <- t_test_result$p.value
    significance <- display_significance(p_value)
  } else {
    # Mann-Whitney-U-Test 
    mwu_test_result <- wilcox.test(data ~ group)
    p_value <- mwu_test_result$p.value
    significance <- display_significance(p_value)
  }
  
  # Store the significance label
  significance_labels <- rbind(significance_labels, data.frame(CpG = cpg, Significance = significance))
}

# Calculate the maximum y-value for positioning significance labels
max_y_value <- max(combined_data$Methylation)
```

```{r}
combined_data$CpG <- factor(combined_data$CpG, levels = unique(combined_data$CpG))

# Definieren Sie Status als Faktor mit gewünschter Reihenfolge der Levels
combined_data$Status <- factor(combined_data$Status, levels = c("Solid Tissue Normal", "Primary solid Tumor"))

# Nun können Sie Ihren Plot erstellen
p <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = CpG, y = Methylation, fill = Status)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "black", outlier.size = 1, width = 0.5, position=position_dodge(width=0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Solid Tissue Normal" = "blue", "Primary solid Tumor" = "red")) +
  labs( x = "CpG sites", y = "beta value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 20),
    plot.margin = margin(25, 25, 25, 25)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.2))) + # Erhöht den Abstand zwischen den Boxen
  geom_text(data = significance_labels, aes(x = CpG, y = max_y_value + 0.05, label = Significance), color = "black", size = 8, inherit.aes = FALSE)

# Plot anzeigen
print(p)

# Plot speichern
ggsave(filename = "plots/BoxPlot_Top7_CpG_Sites_1.pdf", plot = p, width = 20, height = 8)


```

Vergleich Top 5000 CpGs aus Paper1 ( <https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2020.529386> ) mit Top_ranking_CpGs

```{r}
# Laden der benötigten Bibliotheken
install.packages("readxl")
```

```{r}
library(readxl)

library(VennDiagram)

# Dateipfad zur Excel-Datei angeben
file_path <- "C:\\Users\\Irena Dikic\\Downloads\\Table 6.XLSX"  # Passe den Pfad entsprechend deiner Umgebung an tabelle 6 der Supplementary materials paper1

# Excel-Datei einlesen (angenommen, es handelt sich um das erste Blatt)
data <- read_excel(file_path)

# Venn-Diagramm erstellen
venn.diagram(
  x = list(`Top_ranking_CpGs` = Top_ranking_CpGs[1:5000, ]$Name,
           `result` = data$genename),
  category.names = c("Top 5000 CpGs", "Top ranking CpGs paper"),
  filename = "plots/venn_diagram_0.png",
  col = c("skyblue", "purple"),
  category.cex = 1.5,  # Größe der Kategorienamen
  cat.pos = c(0, 0),   # Position der Kategorienamen außerhalb der Kreise
  margin = 0.1,        # Rand um das Diagramm
  fill = c("skyblue", "purple"),
  alpha = 0.5
)

```

```{r}
  cat.pos = c(0, 0),   # Position der Kategorienamen außerhalb der Kreise
  cat.fontfamily = "italic",
  margin = 0.1,     # Rand um das Diagramm
  fill = c("skyblue", "lightgreen"),
  alpha = 0.5,
  ext.pos=c(180,180),
  ext.length = c(0.65,0.85),
  ext.dist = c(0,0.01),
  fontfamily="italic"
)

```

```{r}
# Rang der Gen-Symbole ermitteln
gene_ranks <- match(top_663_DMG_paper,DMR_Genes)

# Ergebnisse anzeigen
result_overlap_663_genes <- data.frame(UCSC_RefGene_Name = top_663_DMG_paper, Rank = gene_ranks)
print(result_overlap_663_genes)

```

```{r}
non_na_result <- result_overlap_663_genes[!is.na(result_overlap_663_genes$Rank), ]

# Ausgeben des gefilterten Dataframes
print(non_na_result)
```

```{r}
# Venn-Diagramm erstellen
venn.diagram(
  x = list(`genes_Top_ranking_CpGs` = DMR_Genes, `genes_result_overlap_663_genes` = top_663_DMG_paper),
  category.names = c("DMR genes", "663 Genes paper"),
  filename = "plots/venn_diagram_2.png",
  col = c("skyblue", "pink"),
  cat.fontfamily = "italic",
  category.cex = 1.5,  # Größe der Kategorienamen
  cat.pos = c(0, 0),   # Position der Kategorienamen außerhalb der Kreise
  margin = 0.1,     # Rand um das Diagramm
  fill = c("skyblue", "pink"),
  alpha = 0.5,
    ext.pos=c(180,180),
  ext.length = c(0.8,0.9),
  ext.dist = c(0,0.01),
  fontfamily="italic"
  
)
```

Vergleich DMR mit Paper2 und Paper3

```{r}
# Laden der erforderlichen Bibliotheken
library(VennDiagram)

# Venn-Diagramm erstellen
venn.diagram(
  x = list(`Top_ranking_CpGs (10000)` = DMR_Genes,
           `result_overlap_663_genes` = top_663_DMG_paper,
           `result_overlap_250_genes` = top_250_DMG_paper),
  category.names = c("DMR genes", "663 genes paper", "250 Top ranking genes paper"),
  cat.fontfamily= "italic",
  filename = "plots/venn_diagram_3.png",
  col = c("skyblue", "pink","lightgreen" ),  # Farben für die drei Kreise
  margin = 0.1,     # Rand um das Diagramm
  fill = c("skyblue", "pink","lightgreen"),  # Füllfarben der Bereiche
  alpha = 0.5,  # Transparenz der Bereiche
  euler.d = TRUE,  # Anzeige von Euler-Diagrammen
  cat.pos = c(-20,20,180),
  fontfamily="italic"
)

```

Wie heißen die 5 Gene, welche in allen 3 datensätzen vorhanden sind

```{r}
# Genes finden, die in allen drei DataFrames vorhanden sind
genes_intersect_all <- Reduce(intersect, list(DMR_Genes,top_663_DMG_paper, top_250_DMG_paper ))

# Ausgabe der Gene
print(genes_intersect_all)

```
